title: Drivers and resolution of inflammaging
bottleneck: Aging brings chronic, sterile, low-grade inflammation (inflammaging) marked by IL-6, TNF-alpha, and CRP, driven by senescent cells, gut leakage, and immune remodeling. But the causal direction is unresolved: is inflammaging a driver of aging or a readout of other damage? Anti-inflammatory trials have mostly treated downstream markers rather than root sources.
why_it_blocks: Inflammaging predicts frailty, cardiovascular disease, dementia, and vaccine failure better than chronological age. If its root drivers cannot be identified and switched off, every age-related disease keeps the same inflammatory fuel.
current_state: Senescent T cells with a senescence-associated secretory phenotype are a confirmed contributor. Lifestyle interventions, Mediterranean diet, and exercise lower inflammatory markers, but no targeted anti-inflammaging therapy is approved. Clinical trials of IL-1beta blockade (CANTOS) reduced cardiovascular events but increased fatal infections, illustrating the double-edged nature of suppressing age-related inflammation.
